newsitem.title: USA: USDA offers $50 Mln supplier credits to Mexico.
newsitem.headline: USDA offers $50 Mln supplier credits to Mexico.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday it was offering $50 million in supplier credit guarantees for sale of ag products to Mexico during fiscal 1997.
The list of eligible products included fruits, vegetables, wine, dairy products, vegetable oils and soy proteins.
The supplier credit guarantee program is an adaptation of the GSM-102 credit guarantee program to assist U.S. exporters who want to provide short-term credits to importers.
USDA also said it amended a GSM-102 offer to Mexico to include planting seeds among the eligible commodities.
Exporters may apply for the supplier credits on a first-come, first-served basis, USDA said. Credit guarantees were available for up to 50 percent of the principal for 15, 20, 30, 45, 60 or 90 days.
USDA said eligible commodities were:
--tree nuts, including almonds, pecans, pistachios, walnuts and hazelnuts.

--fresh fruits, includilng apples, apricots, avocados, blueberries, cherries, grapes, grapefruit, kiwi, lemons, melons, nectarines, oranges, pears, plums, peaches, raspberries, strawberries and tangerines.
--dried fruits, including raisins, prunes, dates and figs.
--canned fruit, including peaches, pears, cocktail and tart cherries.
--potatos, cut and chilled or frozen; flakes and granules.
--fresh vegetables, including asparagus, beans, broccoli, carrots, cauliflower, celery, corn, garlic, lettuce, onions, peppers, potatos and tomatos.
--canned vegetables, including asparagus, beans, carrots, corn, peas, tomatos and tomato paste.
--frozen vegetables, including beans, broccoli, carrots, corn and spinach.
--wine and brandy.

--dairy products, including butter, butter oil, ghee, anhydrous milk fat, nonfat and whole milk powder, whey powder, whey protein concentrate, lactose, non-sweetened condensed milk, fluid milk and cheese.
--ice cream.
--processed meat products such as bacon, deli/sandwich cuts, frankfurters, salami, sausage and similar processed or preserved products.
--pulses, including dry beans, peas and lentils.
--fully refined vegetable oil, including soybean, sunflower, cottonseed, corn and peanuts and blends of them.
--lecithin.
--processed soybean protein products, including flour, grits, protein concentrates and isolates.
--planting seeds.
--commercially prepared cat and dog food.
USDA said $30 million of the supplier guarantee credits would be available immediately. The remainder would be released later.
